column1: # SAMPLE DATA — Pan-India backbone corridors for the LogiRush demonstration network.
# distance_km      approximate road distance along the named corridor (planning figure
# highway_corridor the National Highway / expressway the corridor follows
#                  a descriptive "via" label. Verify against NHAI / MoRTH before operational use.
# road_class       expressway | nh_4lane | nh_2lane | state_highway | hill_road | high_altitude_pass
# terrain_class    primary terrain the corridor crosses; secondary_terrain the next most relevant
#                  (mountain | hill | floodplain | coastal | arid | plains | plateau | forest_remote)
#                  rough physical approximations for the corridor
#                  right (a Himalayan pass is steep and high; a Bihar corridor hugs its rivers).
#                  They are NOT derived from a DEM or a hydrography layer — replace them with
#                  SRTM/Cartosat slope and a river/coast buffer query for a real deployment.
#                  999 = "far" (more than ~200 km) for river and coast distances.
# seasonal_closure_months  typical winter closure window as MM-MM (inclusive
#                  Based on the historically usual window for these passes; the actual opening
#                  and closing dates are announced every year by BRO / the state and vary.
# travel_window    permitted driving hours as HH-HH where movement is routinely restricted at
#                  monsoon advisories). Empty = no routine restriction.
# road_status      baseline status; live changes arrive through verified incident reports.
